addedResources.name: Etalon: Holistic Performance Evaluation Framework for LLM Inference Systems
addedResources.use: Read Sections 2.2, 3.1 and 4.1 with Algorithm 1 and Figures 1 to 3 for TTFT, TBT, TPOT, normalized latency, capacity and fluidity-index; Section 4.2 for black-box and capacity recipes; Section 5.1 for hourly runs over 24 hours and LMSys-Chat-1M medians (417 median, 1418 p90 prefill tokens).

addedResources.name: DistServe: Disaggregating Prefill and Decoding for Goodput-optimized LLM Serving
addedResources.use: Read Section 1 with Figure 1 for per-GPU goodput: the highest request rate served while a target share of requests meets the TTFT and TPOT SLOs (13B model on one A100 reaches about 1.6 requests per second at 90% attainment).

addedResources.name: Nano-vLLM tiny serving engine
addedResources.use: Read `nanovllm/engine/sequence.py` for request state, `scheduler.py` for waiting and running sets, `block_manager.py` for allocate, append, deallocate and prefix-hash reuse, `model_runner.py` for prefill and decode steps, and `llm_engine.py` for the generate and abort path. Trace one request through these files only; do not adopt the engine for load measurement.

addedResources.name: Inference Engineering
addedResources.use: Read Sections 1.4 to 1.4.2 for TTFT, TPS, percentiles and end-to-end versus inference-only time; Section 4.5 with 4.5.1 for benchmark dimensions, tooling and eval inputs; Section 6.1 for vision encoders, image tokens and longer-context effects.

addedResources.name: Gil Tene - How NOT to Measure Latency (talk)
addedResources.use: Use for coordinated-omission vocabulary only: closed-loop testers that wait for each reply, the missing samples under queueing, and the correction concept of recording intended send time. Do not adopt `wrk`, `hey` or `ab`; write the small Python generator in the load-generator unit instead.

study.locator: `apply_chat_template` with role and content dicts, Mistral versus Zephyr control-token examples, `add_generation_prompt` for starting an assistant reply

focus: Identity is model id plus `revision` plus tokenizer plus chat template plus precision. The saved `config.json` fields set shapes; `revision` pins weights.
Dense cost follows total params; MoE per-token cost follows activated params. Attention KV width follows KV heads and head dim, not query heads.
Hybrid layers mix full and local attention; state-space layers keep constant state. Neither takes the full KV formula.
Template control tokens count as input tokens. The wrong template shifts token IDs, lengths and stop behavior.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, write the identity card for Qwen2.5-0.5B (hidden 896, layers 24, heads 14, intermediate 4864, vocab 151936, 494,032,768 params) and derive the invented 64-layer model count \(64 \times 4096 \times (3 \times 16384 + 2 \times 256 \times 40) + 4096 \times 32128 = 18{,}385{,}207{,}296\), about \(18.4 \times 10^9\).
traps: Treating the model name as identity. The same name at another `revision`, tokenizer or template gives different token IDs and lengths.
Reading MoE total params as per-token cost. Only activated experts plus attention run per token; total params set weight bytes.
Applying the MHA cache formula to GQA, MLA or state-space layers. Use KV heads, latent width or constant state as the layer defines.

selfTest.q: Two runs use the same model name but different `revision` values. Can their token IDs be compared?
selfTest.a: No. Weights, tokenizer or template may differ. Record repo id, `revision`, tokenizer and template before comparing any count.

selfTest.q: A MoE model reports 212e9 total params and 31.2e9 activated. Which sets per-token dense work?
selfTest.a: Activated params. Total params set weight bytes; per-token dense work follows the activated path plus attention.

selfTest.q: A layer uses 8 KV heads with head dim 128 in bf16. What is its per-token KV width factor?
selfTest.a: The width uses KV heads: \(2 \times 8 \times 128\) values per layer before layer count and bytes. Query head count does not enter.

selfTest.q: Why does the wrong chat template change serving cost even when the user text is fixed?
selfTest.a: Control tokens become input tokens. They add prefill tokens, change IDs and can change where generation stops.

study.title: Weight bytes and model loading
study.locator: Anatomy of Model's Memory Usage, Model Weights: `bytes = bytes_per_param * num_params` with fp32 4 down to 1-bit 0.125 and MXFP8 1.03125, Llama-3.1-8B bf16 16 GB; Speeding up model loading time with `--load-format npcache` and pre-sharded weights

study.title: Serving arguments that set runtime memory
study.locator: Chapter 2, Serve the LLM (Qwen) with vLLM (pp 57-59): `LLM` with `swap_space`, `max_model_len`, `block_size`, `max_num_seqs`, `prefix_caching` and `cuda_graph` beside `SamplingParams`
study.depth: Read the argument list as the runtime lines to budget. Tuning them belongs to later sections.

focus: Weight bytes are count times stored bytes per value. Execution precision can differ, as int8 weights with bf16 compute, and changes intensity later, not this line.
The file holds more than learned params. GPT-2 holds 137,022,720 values (522.7 MiB in fp32) against 124,439,808 learned params; masks and header explain the gap.
Budget weights first, then KV, then activations, workspace, graphs and allocator. The book reserves about twice model size and still serves one less than theory in Table 5-7.
Activations are megabytes beside gigabytes of cache at long context, but they set the workspace line that stops a theoretical fit from loading.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, derive 7B fp16 as \(7 \times 10^9 \times 2 = 14 \times 10^9\) bytes, 8B bf16 as \(16 \times 10^9\) bytes, 13B bf16 as \(26 \times 10^9\) bytes, and GPT-2 learned versus file as \(124{,}439{,}808 \times 4 = 497{,}759{,}232\) bytes against \(137{,}022{,}720 \times 4 = 548{,}090{,}880\) bytes (522.7 MiB).
traps: Reading the name as the count. Llama-2-7b is about 7e9 params, and its bin reads about 13 GB against the 14 GB product; publish the exact count.
Counting tied embeddings twice. Shared input and output matrices contribute once to weight bytes.
Treating the Table 5-7 quotient as servable. Reserve, workspace, graphs and fragmentation take the last slot; state the overhead line.

selfTest.q: Qwen2.5-0.5B holds 494,032,768 params. What are its bf16 weight bytes?
selfTest.a: \(494{,}032{,}768 \times 2 = 988{,}065{,}536\) bytes, about 0.99 GB. Count tied embeddings once.

selfTest.q: Why does the 7B bin read about 13 GB when the product says 14 GB?
selfTest.a: The name is rounded and the exact count is smaller. The product with the exact count plus header explains the bin; the name alone does not.

selfTest.q: A10 holds 24 GB with 14 GB weights and 4096 context at 0.5 MB per token. Why does it serve 4, not 5?
selfTest.a: \(10 \times 1024 / (0.5 \times 4096) = 5\) in theory, but activations, workspace and allocator take the last slot. The book serves 4 and keeps the reserve explicit.

selfTest.q: When do activations stop being negligible?
selfTest.a: At short context with large batch, where cache per request is small and workspace plus graphs set the limit. At 8192 context they are 80 MB against 6.7 GB cache.

study.title: GQA multiplier, fragmentation and two-regime budget
study.locator: What is stored with `kv_bytes = 2*n_layers*n_kv_heads*head_dim*seq_len*batch*dtype_bytes`; The GQA multiplier with the 70B MHA versus GQA-8 versus MQA table; Fragmentation with 97.6% waste and 20.4-38.2% useful; The two-regime memory budget with crossover at `batch*seq_len = weight_bytes/kv_per_token`

study.title: KV sizing notebook
study.locator: `day05/kv-cache.ipynb`: Memory Cost with `kv_bytes=2*n_layers*n_embd*seq*bytes`, Benchmark 518 ms to 196 ms at length 200, Try These Experiments for slope versus step and 300 and 500 lengths
study.depth: Verify the slope formula independently; the 16 GB per request line for Llama3-8B at 32K context assumes fp16 and full length, so recompute for your precision and length.

focus: KV bytes per token are \(2 \times \text{bytes} \times L \times K \times H\). The shortcut \(4 \times L \times d_{\text{model}}\) assumes KV width equals model width and breaks under GQA and MQA.
Llama-2-7b uses 524,288 bytes per token in fp16; Llama-3.1-8B uses 131,072 bytes in bf16 GQA-8, or 4x with MHA and 8x less with MQA; the invented model uses 262,144 bytes in int8.
MLA compresses keys and values to a latent vector, as in DeepSeek-v3. It is not fewer heads; use latent width for its bytes.
Logical bytes are not servable bytes. Pages, `max_model_len` over-allocation, `reserved_memory` and fragmentation decide the fit; a 200-token request in an 8192 reservation wastes 97.6%.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, derive Llama-2-7b as \(2 \times 32 \times 32 \times 128 \times 2 = 524{,}288\) bytes, Llama-3.1-8B GQA-8 as \(2 \times 32 \times 8 \times 128 \times 2 = 131{,}072\) bytes, and the invented model in int8 as \(2 \times 64 \times 8 \times 256 \times 1 = 262{,}144\) bytes.
traps: Using query heads for KV bytes. Llama-3.1-8B has 32 query heads but 8 KV heads; using 32 overstates bytes by 4x.
Treating MLA as a head count. Its saving comes from latent compression, so recompute from latent width.
Fitting logical bytes. The planner divides \((M - R - M_{\text{model}})\) by per-request bytes with reserve \(R\); omitting \(R\) or page waste overstates batch.

selfTest.q: What are KV bytes per token for a 40-layer, 8 KV head, 128-dim model in int8?
selfTest.a: \(2 \times 40 \times 8 \times 128 = 81{,}920\) bytes.

selfTest.q: The invented model in bf16 uses what per token, and what would full MHA with 32 KV heads use?
selfTest.a: 524,288 bytes in bf16 (262,144 in int8). Full MHA at 32 KV heads would use 2,097,152 bytes in bf16.

selfTest.q: 70B GQA-8 uses 327,680 bytes per token in fp16. What does single-head MQA use?
selfTest.a: 40,960 bytes, an 8x cut. Capacity grows by about 8x before reserve and waste.

selfTest.q: Why does a 200-token request waste 97.6% in an 8192 reservation?
selfTest.a: The reservation holds 8192 times per-token bytes (about 2.5 GiB for 70B) while 200 tokens use 61 MiB. Paging and exact reservation remove most of this.

practice.name: TensorTonic: Plan KV-Cache Capacity
